steps.response:
The image displays an axial cross-section of the thorax with high spatial resolution, clearly distinguishing bone (bright white), soft tissue (gray), and air-filled lung parenchyma (black). This appearance is characteristic of Computed Tomography (CT), specifically a lung window setting given the visibility of pulmonary vasculature and bronchi within the dark lung fields. It is not an X-ray (which would be a projection) or MRI (where cortical bone appears dark).
